To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the multidimensionality of modern psychiatric problems is determined by the development of neurosciences; (2) the development of new classification systems is determined by the need to specify clinical diagnostic criteria; (3) the development of modern psychiatric classifications is characterized by the intensive search for biological background of psychiatric diseases; (4) modern psychiatry is developing in the direction of effective approaches to diagnosis and treatment of psychiatric diseases, as well as in the direction of medical rehabilitation.
the modern psychiatry is in the stage of transition to multidimensional understanding of mental diseases.

modern psychiatry is in the state of active development of the diagnostic and treatment technologies, which is determined by the multidimensionality of mental diseases and necessity to use a combination of different methods for diagnosis and treatment of psychiatric disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) The development of the new classification systems of mental disorders and the necessity of the elaboration of the criteria for the classification of mental disorders in ICD-11; (2) The development of clinical diagnostic criteria for mental disorders; (3) The development of new approaches to the diagnosis of mental disorders; (4) The development of medical rehabilitation programs in psychiatry; (5) The development of a new concept of psychiatry as a science.
the multidimensionality of problems of modern psychiatric and the need to develop classification systems.

the development of the multidimensional model of mental disorders, including the following components: 1) the clinical picture of a disease; 2) the etiology and pathogenesis of the disease; 3) the psychopathological mechanism of the disease; and 4) the psychopathology and psychodynamics of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the development of psychiatry is determined not by the search for a single solution of the problem of the essence of mental disorders, but by a complex of tasks, which are aimed at a more detailed and comprehensive description of the clinical picture of the disease, the development of new diagnostic criteria, the search for the biological basis of mental disorders, and the elaboration of effective methods of treatment and rehabilitation of patients.
the development of modern psychiatric classification systems is a complex and multidirectional process.
modern psychiatry is at the crossroad of the development, and its further progress is possible only with a multidisciplinary approach to the study of psychiatric disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of psychiatry in Russia and in the world is based on the multidimensional approach and the use of the achievements of the neurosciences in the diagnosis and treatment, and the search of biological background for mental disorders.

the modern psychiatry is multidimensional, and the development of the classification systems of mental disorders should be based on the results of the researches in the area of molecular biology, neurosciences, neurochemistry and neuropharmacology.

the development of modern classification systems and the elaboration of new approaches to psychiatric diagnosis are based on the multidimensionality of problems in psychiatry and the necessity of the development of multidimensional approaches to mental diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modern psychiatry is multidimensional.

modern psychiatry is in the process of transition from the era of psychopharmacology and psychosocial approaches to mental health to the era of neurobiology, neuroimaging and genetics of mental disorders.

the development of psychiatry is determined by the necessity of elaboration of new classifications of mental disorders, primarily ICD11, specification of clinical diagnostic criteria, and rethinking of the essence of some psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia.
